messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: HIGH latency and gRPC stream stalls from inference cluster in az1a. Trigger=5xx rate up, tail latency >2s across multiple services. Pager runbook: https://internal/runbooks/az-network-impact

maria_sre: seeing spike on streaming tails. grafana: https://grafana/redwood/streams?panel=tail_latency - lost 30% of healthy connections in az1a since 09:12 UTC.

oncall_jordan: I'm taking this. - checking control plane and route tables. Starting triage.

alex_platform: AWS console shows a high number of ARP retries reported on the hosts in az1a, NIC rx drops and kernel logs: `netdev_recovery: stale arp cache` on a subset of inference hosts.

ryan_network: confirmed, we see abnormal ARP broadcasts from a small host set (eni-0a1b2c3d). Possible ARP table churn causing connection stalls to proxy layer.

maria_sre: quick check - are pods stuck in Terminating / reattach loops? `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` shows steady pod counts. No mass restarts.

alex_platform: control-plane VPC route table for az1a was updated 09:05 for a maintenance change, then rolled back 09:10. I suspect partial state during rollback left some hosts with stale neighbor entries.

oncall_jordan: mitigation plan: 1) isolate noisy ENIs by moving traffic via routing policy to eu-west fallback for new requests; 2) pin longer-lived streams to other AZs; 3) restart affected host agents to flush ARP (rolling, one at a time).

maria_sre: executing policy flip now: `rctl route-set --policy infer-routing --exclude az1a --drain 60s` (will drain new sessions). Notify customers for short degraded tail.

IncidentBot: Route policy change applied by maria_sre at 09:22 UTC. New sessions should route away from az1a.

cust_eng_kate: Kate from Customer Success: started outreach to top affected customers on the list (high-volume inference). Notifying them this is AZ-scoped and mitigation in progress.

ryan_network: starting controlled restart of host eni-0a1b2c3d-agent-7f9: `sudo systemctl restart host-agent` -- monitoring ARP table after.

alex_platform: host restart completed for eni-0a1b2c3d-agent-7f9, ARP entries cleared. Observed drop in rx-drops on that host. Logs: `ip neigh show dev eth0` now stable.

maria_sre: tail latency dropping back towards baseline on regions routed to fallback. Streaming success rate improving from 70% -> 92% for affected routes.

oncall_jordan: initiating phased traffic re-introduction to az1a (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with health checks. Will hold if gRPC error rate climbs.

pm_tom: any customer-facing status update we should push? recommendation: brief note: "We experienced elevated latency and stream failures in a single AZ (az1a). Traffic was temporarily routed away while we flushed host ARP state and mitigated. Most services recovered; we're continuing validation."

cust_eng_kate: sent the customer note. One enterprise customer asked if this could recur; recommending we offer to pin them to Dedicated or multi-AZ routing for SLA-sensitive traffic.

alex_platform: root cause hypothesis: control-plane route change + rollback during maintenance left partial neighbor state on a subset of hosts leading to ARP churn and rx drops. Follow-ups: add preflight blocking for route changes containing active ENIs, and add automated neighbor flush playbook to run during rollbacks.

maria_sre: opened follow-up ticket INFRA-5421 with details and runbook changes.

oncall_jordan: incident status -> mitigated 09:30 UTC, monitoring for 1h. If stable, will close and do postmortem.

IncidentBot: Incident marked MITIGATED by oncall_jordan at 09:30 UTC. Postmortem assignee: maria_sre.

maria_sre: quick notes for postmortem: timeline, affected customer list, traffic redistribution commands, host restart list, and proposed guardrails for route table changes.

pm_tom: thanks team — keep me posted on the postmortem draft and customer followups.

cust_eng_kate: customers updated; one requested an RCA once postmortem is ready.

(Reaction notes: :thumbsup: from pm_tom, :white_check_mark: from alex_platform)
